source.name: U.S. Bankruptcy Court S.D. Florida Administrative Order 2026-06
U.S. Bankruptcy Court S.D. Indiana General Order 26-0004

claim: S.D. Florida AO 2026-06 requires certain court-notice service by designated trustees, debtors' counsel, and unrepresented debtors; for cases filed from October 7, 2026, the commencement/§341 notice must be mailed within three days of the later of the order or clerk's issuance. It requires certificates of service, allows fee-based PACER access to a creditor matrix (with quarterly sub-$30 fee waiver), warns matrices may omit EBN/NCRS addresses, and does not extend statutory or rule deadlines. Unlike Indiana's elective substitute service, this is a mandatory temporary reallocation of service duties, including to some unrepresented parties. No inability to comply or prejudice is established.
falsifier: A superseding order removing the duty, proof that an allegedly affected party was not covered, or evidence of a timely alternative court-directed service path would defeat an asserted burden in that specific case; independently verified inability to comply and consequent missed service would substantiate rather than merely hypothesize the access gap.
firstUnsupportedArrow: Court assigns substitute notice responsibility -> unrepresented debtor can obtain complete recipient information and perform timely legally sufficient service
rivalHypotheses: PACER fee waivers and clerk guidance make substitute notice feasible in many cases.
Already completed lawful service avoids duplicate service.
Court may designate another responsible entity on motion or sua sponte.
Recipient omissions may be corrected through non-BNC records.
The rule's compliance burden does not translate into material practical exclusion for a particular party.
omissions: Original October 16 Florida order was not analyzed in prior October 17 BALA candidate; coverage omission retained.
No paid PACER access, individual case docket, recipient list, personal information or live service attempted.
No actual cost, mail expense, ability-to-pay, failed deadline, motion for relief or recipient prejudice verified.
No independent verification of updated 2026 PACER fee rules beyond text of court order.
negativeResults: CM/ECF continued functioning; lawful NEF service may obviate duplicate notice.
Order provides relief pathways and instructions for unrepresented parties; it does not prove universal exclusion.
Mandatory duty is not equivalent to evidence of nonperformance.
No operative amendment to federal evidence rules or criminal discovery rules inferred.
costBearer: Temporary service labor, mailing, and PACER access fall initially on the designated responsible party unless court relief changes allocation; exact amounts and ultimate legal cost allocation unverified.
